title: Spooky Action at a Distance
content:
is an artist based in Massachusetts.

Meet me at the 2-meter tall bronze statue of Shiva at the Large Hadron Collider:

The Genesis

In March of 2025, I was invited to create a new work for an exhibition in Geneva, Switzerland. The show was slated to be the second edition of the “Art, Games & Society Biennial”, organized by the curatorial team, For The Win. This edition focused on Live Action Role Play or LARP as a point of departure for artwork and performances. A number of artists designed and ran LARP events throughout the run of the show.

This conceit was enticing to me, as the new tradition of LARP is a prime example devirtualization, or phenomena originating in a digital environment that then seeps back into physical space. Previously, collective role-play was categorized as reenactment (of famous battles) or promenade theater (such as Sleep No More). But then after the explosive popularity of Massively Online Role Playing Games (MORPGs) like World of Warcraft, a new desire to collectively act out virtual battles rather than military history emerged. The quality of devirtualization inherent in the design of LARP scenarios opens the floodgates of all manner of inventive participatory play. The title of the exhibition “Side Quests For The Real” gestured toward this dip into virtual worlds and then returning back to the concrete.

During my research phase for the piece, I was pointed towards an essay dissecting the role that Magic Circles play in LARP design. These narrative devices can become physical props that act upon participants or portals through which entities enter the game space. Another analysis of Magic Circles in literature turned me on to the metaphorical potential of creating one of my own. After studying the Le Commun exhibition space from photos and videos, I had the idea to transform two large columns on each floor into emanations sprouting from Magic Circles.

Once I decided on the form the work would take, I pulled together a number of research threads from the past couple years into a comment on technological progression in the modern era: The new tradition of LARP is not trying to emulate a specific historical event (as with reenactments), but rather embody an open-ended and sometimes recursively shifting narrative. In this way, I see LARP as a metaphor for the way that collective belief shapes human development. To illustrate this, I went back to the spooky origin of The British Empire.

Floor 1

In 1582, English mathematician, astronomer and mystic, John Dee produced a circumpolar map of the northern hemisphere. He was an advisor to Queen Elizabeth and presented this map in order to make the case for the expansion of her kingdom. In the map, the vast sea between land masses is rendered as one contiguous form. England’s perch within this form opens the door for the use of naval power to bring anything the sea touches under her domain. Through this cartography, John Dee conceptualized British global conquest that came a hundred or so years later.

At the same time, Dee was engaged in scrying sessions with his medium, Edward Kelley. Together they would enter a trance state and open up a channel to what they believed to be angels. Through this channel a language was revealed that Dee named “Enochian” for the prophet Enoch, who was the only person to have received this angelic disclosure previously. Several books were produced from the “spiritual conferences” dictating all manner of stories, prophecies and instructions. Toward the end of their collaboration, Dee interpreted messages telling him to have intercourse with Kelley’s wife, and so maybe the voices were not from angels but demons. Nevertheless, this practice of scrying, recording, and interpreting was central to Dee’s hermeneutic quest for a universal knowledge of all things.

Dee’s wax decoder disk is one of the few surviving artifacts from these divination sessions. The disk was used to translate Enochian into discernible text. I brought together an adaptation of the disk and the circumpolar map into one vinyl graphic surrounding the bottom floor column. I wanted to mash up these two incredibly consequential elements of John Dee’s biography into one and create a Magic Circle from which our knotty view of modernity springs forth.

Column 1

Rising upwards from the Dee’s circle we find Promethean Flames of creation. In 1816 the earth was wrapped in dreary rain clouds as a result of a volcano eruption in Indonesia. During “The Year Without A Summer” Mary Shelley visited Lord Byron at Villa Diodati, overlooking Lake Geneva. The house where she experienced a “waking dream” that sparked the gothic horror of “Frankenstein or, The Modern Prometheus” is not more than a fifteen minute drive from this installation. I visited this location on my last evening in Geneva. At dusk twisting trees scrape a rolling navy sky.

The damask flames alchemize into a band of Lysergic acid diethylamide, commonly known as LSD, Acid or Lucy. This molecule was first synthesized from ergot in 1938 and its consciousness shifting properties were discovered in Basel, Switzerland in 1943 by Albert Hofmann. In the second half of the 20th century, mass-production and dissemination of LSD re-ordered psychological paradigms. The supercharged perceptions of trippers influenced everything from the development of the internet to enhanced torture practices. Here, the LSD molecule is rendered using a digital hallucinatory tool, GAN-imagery. Stare at it long enough and fractal symmetries will emerge inside your mind's eye.

Rising high above your head is a taxonomy of UFO experiencers’ first-hand accounts. Bubbles, cigars, saucers and balls of light twist and hover from within a field of energy. The phenomenon of UFO sightings, and later, alien abductions sit at the heart of post-war paranoia. Swiss sociologist, Carl Jung, described the phenomenon as an unconscious yearning for oneness during a moment of great fracture in the west. In “Flying Saucers” 1959, he describes how rings of glowing beacons resemble the mandala, an eastern symbol for unity. In my view, the attempt at categorization and cataloging of these impossible objects is a modern day instantiation of an angelic language, with orbs, shadows and blinking color scattered across time and space, challenging us to connect the pieces and uncover the message.

Floor 2

The installation penetrates the second floor by breaking the barrier of the present and extending up into the future. The ceaseless march of history is resonated by a second Magic Circle. In white matte vinyl, I have constructed a propositional underground map of The Future Circular Collider (FCC), CERN’s plan for the next half-century of physics research. A smaller ring denotes the footprint of the currently operating Large Hadron Collider, a superstructure experiment running near-lightspeed particle collisions around the clock to unlock the secrets of the universe.

I became intrigued by The FCC proposal for a number of reasons. It originally called for new nuclear power plants to be built in order to power it, but after much controversy, that part of the plan was dropped and now the project’s proponents simply believe that by the time construction is complete a brand new decarbonized grid will be operational and ready to juice it up. There is so much hyperstitional hope wrapped up in this plan. A scientist recently criticized the plan, saying that similar particle physics break-throughs could be achieved through a linear construction. I am obsessed with the idea that the dedication to a circular formation borders on religious worship. The symbol of a $40 billion circular mega-project soaking up research funding for generations to come, makes me think of it as a hyper-object or an entity that has taken on a sense of agency and is bending the future towards its will.

The inner boundary of The FCC circle is made up of the various territories, cantons and districts in Switzerland and France that would be effected by its construction. The massive scale of the underground collider tunnel would require changes to building locations, energy production and land use. The middle of the diagram is a representation of the particle collisions happening at CERN. I dug into the institute’s monthly magazine archive stretching back to the 60s, to find early depictions of these experiments. There is something so poetic in the chaotic collisions producing devolutions to theoretical particles at a once-in-a-billion chance. The collider is a project of world creation, recreating the conditions of the Big Bang to peer back into the impossible, a time before time, before matter. This is the same pursuit as Dee, but instead of obsidian black scrying mirrors we gaze into endless streams of data collected from chaos.

A red star on the map represents the location of Geneva. The pattern of the star is calls upon the design of Geneva’s medieval fortress walls.

Column 2

CERN is responsible for many scientific breakthroughs. Outside the field of particle physics and origin of the universe research, the institute has helped push forward nuclear power and nuclear medicine. In addition, and perhaps most pertinent to artistic expression, is the fact that it was at CERN that Sir Tim Berners Lee first conceptualized and programmed a network of interconnected computers that kicked-off “The Internet” as we know it today. I wanted to represent the dynamic of collective belief in scientific breakthrough leading to resource allocation that directs parallel technological developments and so I collaged images of construction projects from photos I have taken in the past five years documenting the rapid development of my neighborhood in Allston, Massachusetts. The tangle of scaffolding, cranes and concrete skeletons springs up from the CERN Circle.

60% of the world’s capital is now tied up in Real Estate development. And yet, many of the world’s inhabitants live in subpar shelters or are “rent-burdened” (when over 30% of income goes to rent). This situation illustrates the reality that these domiciles are not being built for human utility but as speculative investment. A system that has overrun its own logic and devolved into a kind of LARP: real structures made of steel and concrete housing imagined residents only seen in 3D renders for promotional material.

Emerging out of the scaffolding are digital stacks. Overlaid informational nodes fragment and glisten in the blue light glow. Infinite holographic media erects a digital twin of reality and every possible permutation is played out inside the ceaseless whir of the server room. How can we represent the cloud? How can we bring it back down to earth? The datacenters are off limits and even if we could experience the unending growl of cooling configurations it would not bring us closer to grasping the planetary computation happening inside. We are blinkered by blinking lights. The images we use to visualize Big Data are downstream from Silicon Valley pitch decks, a Frutiger Aero fantasy of sliding glass crystals, ever interchangeable and perfect. There is no Real reality there and so the closest we can get is LARP. We must sync our actions with the oscillations of dark patterns and ride the algorithm back to the source.

Our journey upwards into the far future or distant past will always end with the sun. Our sun is not just a star, it is our home and our destiny. Will we be able to master its fusion combustion and reach an escape velocity of civilizational development before its stored potential energy cooks us once and for all? We must make more suns, many suns, a sun in every home in order to achieve a brokered peace with cosmic thermodynamics. This is where I believe so-called “Artificial Intelligence” is leading us. We are not so much as racing towards a bright future of peace and freedom from want, but rather entering a time-loop back towards a re-enchanted relationship to nature, it’s Medieval Times 2.0, except now, we are all John Dee necromancing the combined knowledge of the past. Sufficiently complex technology is indistinguishable from Magic, and so, will it be a dark magick or can we find our way to the light?
author: Do Not Research
